body:
### Summary

When `uv pip install --overrides` is given a requirements file whose path contains a space, uv appears to split the path at the space, despite the path being passed as a single quoted argument.

I noticed this bug when attempting to upgrade Unsloth Studio using their PowerShell installer script. My user name has a space (`Damon Lynch`), which was causing the installer to fail. I used ChatGPT to help me isolate the issue.  The minimal reproduction below is from me.

### Minimal Reproduction

```
$dir ="D:\uv test"
uv venv $dir
$override = Join-Path $dir "override.txt"
Set-Content -LiteralPath $override -Value "idna==3.10"
uv pip install ` --python "D:\uv test\Scripts\python.exe" ` --overrides "$override" ` --dry-run ` requests
error: File not found: `D:\uv`
```

Perhaps of interest is that the `--python` path does not need to contain a space to reproduce the problem. For example, with a Python executable at a space-free path:
```
uv pip install ` --python "D:\UVTEST~1\Scripts\python.exe" ` --overrides "$override" ` --dry-run ` requests
error: File not found: `D:\uv`
```

For comparison, the same installation works when the override file is located at a path containing no spaces, e.g. dir `uv-test`:
```
$dir ="D:\uv-test"
uv venv $dir
$override = Join-Path $dir "override.txt"
Set-Content -LiteralPath $override -Value "idna==3.10"
uv pip install ` --python "D:\uv-test\Scripts\python.exe" ` --overrides "$override" ` --dry-run ` requests
```

It seems to me that uv should treat the value passed to `--overrides` as a single path, regardless of spaces in that path, and successfully read the requirements file.


### Platform

Windows 11 x64

### Version

uv 0.12.9 (9f9286029 2026-09-01 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

### Python version

Python 3.14.7
title: Windows: uv pip install --overrides fails when requirements file path contains spaces
